📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

In a recent development, one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

It has been revealed that italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Sources indicate that van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which shows his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their new deals.

Alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing glitch for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

It was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

According to recent reports, slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

According to recent reports, he is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

The Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

According to recent reports, confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

It has been revealed that in the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

Sources indicate that in the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

Since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Big Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a new-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Liverpool need to see more from their major-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that il Napoli di Allegri respira e torna a vincere, finalmente. Dopo aver creato e anche corso qualche rischio di troppo in una gara a lungo dominata, gli azzurri contro il Torino si aggiudicano i tre punti grazie ad una gran botta del solito McTominay. L'ultima vittoria degli azzurri risaliva al 28 ottobre, nel 4-1 al Monza. Allegri respira, anche se perde pure Vergara. Per contro Abate vede fermarsi Belghali e Ismajli, così come il suo Toro, protagonista di una gara comunque combattuta, ma nella quale non ha saputo nemmeno questa volta raccogliere.

Allegri lascia in panchina De Bruyne, scegliendo Anguissa, Gilmour e McTominay in mediana e Vergara in appoggio a Hojlund. Dall'altra parte resta fuori Vlasic, non al meglio dopo gli impegni con la Croazia: chance per Gineitis con Braganca e Mandragora in mediana, con Che Adams che torna titolare vicino a Simeone.

According to recent reports, il Napoli crea tanto e spreca nei primi 45 minuti. McTominay va come un trattore, in un quarto d'ora impegna due volte Perri e manda in porta Politano - fermato dal portiere granata - spedendo poi fuori il tap-in. Anche Hojlund è ben presente ed esalta a sua volta i riflessi del portiere granata, sfiorando il gol anche di testa.

All'11' si ferma Vergara, che esce in lacrime per un problema al flessore. Al suo posto De Bruyne: il belga entra bene e a sua volta ha una grande chance, ma di testa centra Coco da pochi pass. Pericoloso anche Anguissa. Dal lato opposto problema per Belghali al 40' (dentro Aboukhal), forse connesso a quello avuto al ginocchio, in nazionale. I granata sono pericolosi con un tiro di Gineitis controllato da Milinkovic-Savic e soprattutto con una traversa di Mandragora.

Sources indicate that abate inserisce subito Vlasic per Braganca nell'intervallo. Aboukhlal va vicino al palo ad inizio ripresa, poi Marin pasticcia e Vlasic va vicino al vantaggio. McTominay impegna ancora Perri dai venti metri. Milinkovic-Savic risponde alla punizione di Mandragora. Allegri lancia Lang e Olivera (per Spinazzola e Marin). Perri ne prende altre tre in dieci minuti: sullo stesso Lang, poi su Politano e Hojlund.

Il Napoli riesce al 72': Lang recupera palla da terzino vero su Aboukhlal, poi serve McTominay che dal limite la incastra all'angolino con un gran destro. L'ultimo tratto di partita serve al Napoli per calmare le sfuriate del Toro e portare a casa tre punti che portano respiro.

Così il tecnico del Napoli, Massimiliano Allegri, in conferenza stampa: "Vergara si è fatto male, non so per quanto lo perderemo. Dispiace molto, era molto abbattuto. Credo sia stato un infortunio per il periodo, quest'anno ha responsabilità diverse, la Nazionale, maggiori pressioni mentali... Questi infortuni a volte sono causati anche da queste cose. La partita? I ragazzi sono stati molto bravi, hanno avuto l'umiltà e il rispetto di mettersi al pari del Torino. La squadra si è comportata bene anche nelle fasi finali della partita, sui calci d'angolo. Ci dà più solidità non prendere gol stasera, erano 8 partite che subivamo gol".

Così invece l'allenatore del Torino, Ignazio Abate: "Rimane rammarico, le buone prestazioni non bastano, potevamo fare qualcosa in più per prendere punti. Nel secondo tempo sembrava che stessimo prendendo in mano la partita nei primi 20-25 minuti, ma lì dovevamo avere la forza di andare in vantaggio".

Le dichiarazioni del tecnico Eusebio Di Francesco per analizzare il momento della squadra.

Nel prepartita di Lazio-Lecce, il tecnico dei giallorossi, Eusebio Di Francesco, ha fatto il punto della situazione intervenendo ai microfoni di Dazn.

In a recent development, torna la Serie A dopo la pausa per le Nazionali: ci si aspettano cambiamenti, ma arrivano per lo più conferme. In primis dalla capolista Lazio, che vince e mantiene il primo posto solitario. Successo anche per i cugini della Roma, momentaneamente secondi in classifica in attesa del risultato dell'Inter contro l'Atalanta. Giornata positiva anche per il Como, che riscatta la caduta contro i nerazzurri di Chivu avvenuta subito prima della sosta.

Industry observers note that se per le tre squadre appena citate le prime posizioni sono ormai una sorta di giardino di casa, lo stesso non si può dire per il Napoli visto il suo complicato inizio di stagione. La vittoria del Maradona, però, consente ai partenopei di intravedere la zona europea. Restano a metà classifica Cagliari e Torino, battute rispettivamente dal Como e dagli azzurri di Allegri. Nella parte bassa della graduatoria, pesanti le sconfitte per Lecce (3-0 a Roma contro la Lazio) e Parma (battuto 1-5 in casa dalla Roma). Eventuali risultati positivi delle concorrenti possono rendere vicinissima la zona retrocessione per salentini e ducali.

Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4376 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • Recent findings suggest that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • Recent findings suggest that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Recent findings suggest that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

In a recent development, ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Recent findings suggest that for the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

Recent findings suggest that “It reveals where we have potential,” he remarked. “There are elements to improve offensively.

Sources indicate that “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads highlighted major character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

Recent findings suggest that A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a latest manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

Sources indicate that when Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It has been revealed that it is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

It has been revealed that that opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

In a recent development, bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Industry observers note that tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Recent findings suggest that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

Sources indicate that that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

Industry observers note that “We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads revealed the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV.

"Since the fresh manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE.

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

According to recent reports, dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

It has been revealed that smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

It has been revealed that the noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Sources indicate that amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

In a recent development, bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Recent findings suggest that scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

Sources indicate that the current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Recent findings suggest that safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

Sources indicate that the pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

In a recent development, jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

According to recent reports, it looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

It has been revealed that newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Sources indicate that newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

In a recent development, wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

In a recent development, just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

In a recent development, newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm.

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF.

Industry observers note that there will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0.

Recent findings suggest that st James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under fresh head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Sources indicate that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. Upcoming signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Sources indicate that marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

It has been revealed that at opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

In a recent development, domani sera contro l'Atalanta dovrebbe scendere in campo un 'tridente' inedito tra le file dell'Inter: agiranno dalla parte destra infatti Benjamin Pavard, Djed Spence e Pio Esposito per la prima volta insieme in stagione. Si sofferma su questo oggi La Gazzetta dello Sport: "Una catena di destra nuova di zecca, composta da un tris di anelli brillanti e pronti a continuare a splendere o a tornare a farlo. Soggettivo, dipende dai casi. Dal rigenerato Pavard al confermato Spence, arrivando fino al gioiello Pio Esposito: per la prima volta in stagione, Cristian Chivu dovrebbe scegliere questi tre interpreti per costruire la fascia destra. Il francese nel terzetto dei difensori davanti a Martinez, l'ex Tottenham sempre più determinante a tutta fascia, Pio pronto a ricevere.

It has been revealed that tre uomini che mai prima di oggi hanno giocato insieme, né dall’inizio né un po' più per caso a gara in corso, se non per la manciata di minuti finale di Rotterdam quando Pavard subentrò nel finale della sfida di Champions sul campo del Feyenoord con la partita ormai in cassaforte. Poco, pochissimo, per farsi un'idea concreta. Ma abbastanza per provare a comprendere quale sia il piano tattico nella mente dell'allenatore nerazzurro per la sfida alla Dea. Se l'impiego di Pavard rappresenterebbe una novità - gradita scandagliando i pochi precedenti - non sorprenderà invece rivedere Djed Spence padrone della corsia destra. L'inglese ha ormai scavalcato Andy Diouf nelle gerarchie in corsia, garantisce meno fantasia offensiva ma più abitudine nel difendere. È stato acquistato in estate per questo (ad una cifra importante) e non è un caso che ormai partirà stabilmente avanti rispetto al francese. Davanti, a proposito di profili internazionali e graditi in Europa e nel mondo, l'Inter non può rinunciare a Pio Esposito: 5 gol nelle ultime 4 partite tra nerazzurro e Nazionale, una forma ritrovata al top, la possibilità di gestire con calma il ritorno in campo di Lautaro Martinez.

Industry observers note that comprendere come si muoverebbe sul campo una catena tutta nuova è ad oggi parecchio complesso, considerando che il campione da cui pescare spunti tattici vari lascia lo spazio della manciata di minuti di Rotterdam in cui Pavard, Spence ed Esposito si sono ritrovati in campo insieme nello stesso momento. Ma qualche certezza c'è: Pavard, nato terzino, potrà sfruttare la diligenza difensiva di Spence per uscire ed alzarsi a seconda dei momenti, e non è escluso nemmeno che in determinate fasi i due possano persino alternarsi. Il resto diventa un tema più che altro offensivo, perché se Esposito arriva da 5 gol consecutivi di cui un paio nelle ultime 2 con l'Inter, il merito va spartito proprio con Djed Spence: assist (sporcato) dell'inglese a Rotterdam per il 94 nerazzurro in Champions League e altro passaggio vincente per indirizzare rapidamente la sfida di campionato contro il Como. Un'intesa fruttuosa e in crescendo, a cui l'Inter non può rinunciare", conclude la Rosea.

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its fresh ambassador.

According to recent reports, now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’.

BC.GAME, an online casino organization, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Leicester City have axed a partnership with BC.GAME, after the gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador.

Leicester confirmed fans who have purchased a replica shirt featuring the sponsor's name within the last 28 days can return it for a full refund or exchange by December 2.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too.

In recent years, Leicester’s spectacular decline on the pitch has mirrored the relationship with their supporters.

During the years immediately before and after their stunning Premier League triumph in 2016, it was difficult to find a club more in tune with the fanbase.

But a series of baffling decisions – including the tie-up with BC.GAME – eroded trust between the club and their supporters.

Leicester are now in League One and face a long road back but sensible moves like this one suggest they are at least facing in the right direction again.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il Milan è pronto a investire nel mercato di gennaio, ma senza rinunciare alla programmazione.
  • According to recent reports, L'allenatore portoghese non ha escluso l'arrivo di un altro attaccante: “Un'opzione in più potrebbe essere una buona cosa per aiutare Camarda e Ramos”, ha spiegato Amorim, sottolineando come la squadra faccia ancora troppa fatica ad arrivare nell'ultimo terzo di campo.
  • It has been revealed that il Milan segue da tempo il già citato Endrick, per il quale il Real Madrid potrebbe valutare anche una cessione definitiva con diritto di riacquisto.

Il Milan è pronto a investire nel mercato di gennaio, ma senza rinunciare alla programmazione. A confermarlo è stato Gerry Cardinale, presente a Milanello in occasione della conferenza stampa di Ruben Amorim alla vigilia della sfida con il Frosinone. Il proprietario di RedBird ha ribadito le intenzioni della società: “Spenderemo, ma lo faremo in modo intelligente. E sempre con il quadro generale del progetto in mente, a stretto contatto con mister Amorim”. Tra gli obiettivi c'è anche Endrick, per il quale Cardinale ha avuto parole importanti: “È tra i migliori giocatori al mondo, se non il migliore, nel suo ruolo. Lo rispetto tanto. Vedremo cosa succederà sul mercato”.

According to recent reports, L'allenatore portoghese non ha escluso l'arrivo di un altro attaccante: “Un'opzione in più potrebbe essere una buona cosa per aiutare Camarda e Ramos”, ha spiegato Amorim, sottolineando come la squadra faccia ancora troppa fatica ad arrivare nell'ultimo terzo di campo. Il tecnico ha difeso Gonçalo Ramos, convinto che il centravanti possa segnare molto di più se messo nelle condizioni giuste. Sui possibili investimenti, però, ha invitato alla prudenza: “Non vogliamo una grande stella, ma un ragazzo equilibrato, che arrivi qui per essere parte integrante della squadra”. La preferenza è per un giocatore giovane, funzionale al progetto e non necessariamente già affermato.

It has been revealed that il Milan segue da tempo il già citato Endrick, per il quale il Real Madrid potrebbe valutare anche una cessione definitiva con diritto di riacquisto. Le cifre ipotizzate arrivano a 60 milioni di euro più 10 di bonus, mentre l'alternativa principale resta Nicolò Tresoldi del Bruges. Sullo sfondo anche la possibilità che Francesco Camarda parta in prestito: sebbene Amorim abbia preferito rinviare ogni valutazione a gennaio, la decisione pare già presa. Cardinale ha poi confermato i contatti per il rinnovo di Adrien Rabiot: “Stiamo parlando e spero di arrivare presto a un lieto fine. Penso che debba essere un giocatore simbolo del Milan”. Sul prossimo arrivo di Markus Krosche, invece, nessuna conferma: la società comunicherà eventuali novità soltanto quando sarà pronta.

Breaking: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

It has been revealed that the substantial moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

It has been revealed that on this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams remarked: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” noted Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

Recent findings suggest that while Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

According to recent reports, one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi noted: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something crucial.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with massive qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi stated: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

The substantial headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more crucial to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

Sources indicate that “I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just mentioned he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very crucial that he is with us.”.

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi looks to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Industry observers note that palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona sporting director Deco has left the door wide open for Liverpool to sign Ronald Araujo permanently.

The Uruguayan joined the Reds on a season-long loan in August and has made an immediate impression on the Anfield faithful, putting in a series of tremendous performances at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Reports from Spain in recent days have indicated that Merseyside chiefs are keen to take up the option to sign the defender outright for £47m, with the player also understood to be ready to stay in L4 beyond next summer.

Liverpool’s chances of securing him on a permanent basis would appear to have been greatly boosted by comments from Deco.

Recent findings suggest that the Barcelona chief told Catalunya Radio’s Tot Costa: “A bit of money wouldn’t hurt us either. We’d be happy because things have gone well, and we’d be happy for him too.

“Personally, I’m happy for Ronald. He’s one of the team’s leaders. He’s been through some difficult times and some happy ones at the club, and we have a good relationship.

It has been revealed that “He’s made his decision, and we respect it. The most important thing for us is to see him happy. If he decides to stay and things carry on like this, we’d be happy with that too.”.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images).

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It seems that, if Liverpool were to sign Araujo permanently, everyone would be a winner.

The Reds would secure a player who’s been excellent for them (and get a deal done at a relatively modest fee), the defender would get to remain on Merseyside (where his family are reportedly very happy), and Barcelona would bank nearly £50m for someone they’re seemingly happy to let go.

Even with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni finally back in first-team training, both of them will realistically need a few more weeks to be properly matchday ready, so Iraola will continue to depend heavily on the Uruguayan to maintain form and fitness.

Liverpool won’t be able to activate the purchase option on Araujo until the end of the season, and it’s not implausible that he could succumb to a serious injury or see his performance levels drop in the meantime.

Industry observers note that right now, though, there’s no excuse for Anfield chiefs not to go all-out to secure a permanent transfer, especially with Deco indicating that Barcelona would be prepared to sanction his sale. Don’t fumble this one please, Julian Ward!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il tecnico dei salentini è intervenuto ai microfoni nel post partita dopo la sconfitta per 3-0 contro la Lazio.

All’Olimpico il match che apre la 12ª giornata di campionato di Serie A finisce 3-0 per la Lazio, trascinata dalla doppietta decisiva di Tijjani Noslin e dal gol di Frattesi, contro un Lecce ordinato nella prima frazione ma calato alla distanza nella ripresa. I biancocelesti consolidano così il primo posto in classifica e allungano momentaneamente a +4 dall’Inter, impegnata domani a Bergamo. Nonostante alcuni infortuni, i capitolini mettono in campo una prestazione brillante e conquistano i tre punti con autorità. Al termine della partita, il mister dei salentini Eusebio Di Francesco è stato intervistato ai microfoni di DAZN.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il risultato è troppo rotondo per la partita e per i valori che ci sono stati. Abbiamo subito tre occasioni da gol e preso tre gol. Il primo tempo è stato ottimo e non siamo riusciti a concretizzare delle situazioni. Dopo il 2-0 la gara si è messa in salita. Credo che la gara sia stata buona, i valori sono differenti e non meritavamo questo risultato. Si perdono poi le sicurezze, ci sta abbassarsi contro la Lazio. Lì dovevamo difendere meglio e cercare il riferimento. Noslin ha saltato con troppa libertà, era il primo tiro della Lazio, abbiamo lavorato bene con la linea. Loro hanno poi il motore della squadra e subisci le ripartenze. Abbiamo preso dei gol di troppo, anche ingenui sul terzo. Eravamo disordinati all’88’. Mi dà fastidio aver preso anche il terzo gol anche se eravamo poco lucidi.

Sources indicate that noi li sosteniamo ma devono fare qualcosa in più, abbiamo bisogno della loro disponibilità. Ti trovi la Lazio che ti pressa e devi mettere in profondità palle meno pulite. Gli esterni hanno fatto cose interessanti ma poi devi dare la sensazione di poter far male. Ora devo capire se dare più forza da una parte all’altra. Mi aspetto qualcosa di più da loro d’ora in poi.

Il gradimento di Luciano Spalletti, allenatore della Juventus, verso le qualità di Ndour resta un tema destinato a riaffiorare, ma strappare il 22enne alla Fiorentina già a gennaio appare estremamente complicato: la società viola - secondo quanto rivelato da La Repubblica di Firenze - non ha alcuna intenzione di privarsi di un perno tattico nel pieno della risalita in classifica, a maggior ragione nel bel mezzo della stagione in corso. Qualsiasi discorso relativo al futuro sarebbe rinviato semmai all'estate, specialmente se per alcune prestazioni dovesse lievitare la sua valutazione.

In a recent development, la Juventus lavora per rinforzare il reparto offensivo in vista del mercato di gennaio e guarda con particolare interesse all'Atletico Madrid. Al centro dei contatti tra i due club ci sarebbe un possibile scambio tra Jonathan David e Alexander Sorloth, operazione che potrebbe soddisfare le esigenze di entrambe le società. Come riportato dalla Gazzetta dello Sport, Luciano Spalletti vorrebbe aggiungere un attaccante alla propria rosa, mentre Diego Simeone sarebbe disposto a rinunciare definitivamente a uno dei due. Una convergenza di interessi che potrebbe favorire la trattativa, anche se restano da superare alcune divergenze sulle valutazioni economiche dei due giocatori. Il nome di Alexander Sorloth non è nuovo negli ambienti bianconeri. L'attaccante norvegese era già stato accostato alla Juventus durante la scorsa estate, quando avrebbe raggiunto un'intesa di massima con il club e avuto un confronto diretto con Spalletti. La possibilità di trasferirsi a Torino sarebbe ancora gradita al centravanti, che in questa prima parte di stagione non ha trovato la via del gol con la continuità sperata. A favorire un'eventuale partenza potrebbe essere anche la situazione contrattuale: Sorloth è legato all'Atletico fino al giugno 2028, con il club spagnolo intenzionato a evitare il rischio di perderlo a parametro zero in futuro. Discorso differente per Jonathan David, arrivato alla Juventus in prestito dall'Atletico e fin qui mai decisivo. Il canadese avrebbe invece ritrovato continuità e fiducia durante la sua esperienza in Spagna, conquistando la stima di Simeone grazie a tre gol, oltre alle prestazioni e all'atteggiamento mostrati in campo. L'Atletico sarebbe quindi disposto a valutare un'operazione che consenta di trattenere definitivamente l'ex Lille, mentre la Juventus potrebbe sfruttare l'accordo per portare Sorloth a Torino.

La Juventus torna a guardare in casa Tottenham per risolvere l'emergenza sulla corsia mancina a gennaio. Forte dei solidi rapporti internazionali intessuti dall'amministratore delegato Giovanni Carnevali - decisivo in estate per chiudere in extremis le operazioni Vicario e Sarr - grazie anche all'intermediazione di Edoardo Crnjar, l'imminente ingresso di Piero Ausilio nei quadri dirigenziali degli Spurs spingerebbero Destiny Udogie in bianconero. L'ex Udinese non è mai riuscito a entrare pienamente nei meccanismi tattici di Roberto De Zerbi, raccogliendo appena 5 presenze in Premier League: una marginalità che spinge il club londinese ad aprire alla cessione a titolo temporaneo. La formula del prestito oneroso con diritto di riscatto rappresenta la soluzione ideale per il tandem Carnevali-Massara, chiamato a gestire con oculatezza il budget invernale dopo aver già stanziato risorse importanti per regalare a Luciano Spalletti un nuovo centravanti. L'operazione Udogie metterebbe d'accordo tutte le componenti in gioco: permetterebbe al tecnico di Certaldo di avere un esterno duttile in entrambe le fasi sul quale aveva puntato con convinzione già ai tempi della Nazionale, a Carnevali di proseguire la ricostruzione di uno zoccolo duro italiano nello spogliatoio bianconero e offrirebbe allo stesso giocatore una vetrina (Serie A ed Europa League) per rilanciarsi e riconquistare il giro degli Azzurri.

L'Inter comincia a programmare le strategie per il mercato di gennaio, tra possibili rinforzi e cessioni necessarie per finanziare nuovi investimenti. Tra i giocatori che potrebbero lasciare Milano figura anche Luis Henrique, esterno brasiliano arrivato durante l'ultima sessione estiva e finora incapace di ritagliarsi un ruolo centrale nel progetto tecnico di Cristian Chivu. Come riportato dal Corriere della Sera, la dirigenza nerazzurra sta valutando alcune operazioni in uscita per reperire le risorse economiche necessarie a intervenire sul mercato. Il nome del brasiliano rientra tra quelli presi in considerazione, anche se al momento non risultano trattative concrete per una sua eventuale cessione.

It has been revealed that il futuro di Bruno Fernandes è destinato a far parlare ancora mesi, specialmente dopo le antenne sollevate dal Milan nel percepire più di qualche distanza tra il capitano portoghese e il club dei Red Devils per raggiungere l'intesa e stipulare il rinnovo. Le trattative sono aperte, ma non si sono registrati - almeno fino a questo momento - passi avanti o svolte determinanti, per questo l'ex Udinese potrebbe anche pensare di lasciare il club inglese. Il giocatore di 32 anni è legato ai Red Devils da un contratto valido fino al giugno 2027, tuttavia esiste un'opzione unilaterale di estensione fino al 2028 in favore dello United, che manterrebbe attiva una clausola rescissoria da circa 65 milioni di euro. Fino a questo momento, tuttavia, Bruno Fernandes avrebbe già rifiutato due offerte di rinnovo e questo pone riflessioni sul suo destino. Mentre i Red Devils hanno faticato negli ultimi anni, Bruno Fernandes è riuscito a strappare risultati con prestazioni trascinanti e la scorsa stagione ha superato anche le più rosee aspettative, segnando 9 gol e realizzando 21 assist in Premier League. Superando così un certo David Beckham in questo record personale di passaggi chiave. Ma cosa pensa dei rumor lo United? Ne ha parlato l'amministratore delegato Omar Berrada a Sky Sports UK: "Abbiamo un enorme rispetto per Bruno. Siamo molto fortunati ad averlo come capitano. Quello che ha fatto per questa squadra negli ultimi sei, sette anni è assolutamente incredibile. L'anno scorso ha vinto, credo, tutti i premi individuali che si possono vincere. E siamo molto orgogliosi di averlo come capitano. È vero che stiamo avendo conversazioni sul suo nuovo contratto, ma preferisco mantenerle riservate. Credo che sia qualcosa che vada discusso dietro le quinte tra lui e il club".

Industry observers note that dalla Spagna rimbalzano conferme sempre più insistenti sul destino di Nico Paz: il Real Madrid ha ormai deciso di riportare alla base il talento argentino in vista della stagione 2027-2028. Dopo aver rinunciato la scorsa estate all'opzione di recompra da 9 milioni di euro, incassando invece dal Como altri 60 milioni, la dirigenza merengue è ora pronta a esercitare il nuovo diritto di riacquisto fissato a 80 milioni di euro. Secondo quanto riferito da Deportes COPE e precisato dal quotidiano MARCA, il presidente del Real Florentino Perez potrà attivare ufficialmente la clausola in una finestra temporale ben definita, compresa tra l'1 e il 15 luglio 2027. Il ritorno al Santiago Bernabeu alla corte di José Mourinho resta tuttavia strettamente dipendente dalla volontà del calciatore, che nelle ultime settimane ha continuato a brillare tra la Champions League con i lariani e la nazionale argentina. Già in estate Nico Paz aveva scelto di proseguire il proprio percorso di crescita agli ordini di Cesc Fabregas proprio per evitare di restare chiuso da una concorrenza stellare dai blancos. Tra Kylian Mbappé, Vinicius Junior, Jude Bellingham, Brahim Díaz, Diomande, Endrick e il lungodegente Rodrygo, il 10 del Como pretenderà garanzie tecniche e di spazio concrete prima di accettare il trasferimento.

Sul fronte internazionale, il Manchester United torna a pensare a Victor Osimhen. L'arrivo di Mauricio Pochettino ha riacceso l'interesse dei Red Devils per l'ex Napoli, che sarebbe disposto a valutare un trasferimento in Premier League. Il Galatasaray, però, non intende fare sconti: il nigeriano ha un contratto fino al 2029 e una valutazione compresa tra 80 e 100 milioni di euro. Un'operazione complicata per gennaio, più percorribile in estate. Il Napoli conserva il 10% sulla futura rivendita. Intanto, proprio allo United, resta in bilico Amad Diallo: l'ivoriano vuole maggiore continuità e piace ad Aston Villa e Besiktas. Tra i possibili partenti figurano anche Zirkzee, Dalot e De Ligt.

Il Crystal Palace valuta invece il ritorno in Premier League di Ivan Toney. L'attaccante inglese, protagonista in Arabia Saudita con l'Al Ahli, è un obiettivo per gennaio e potrebbe ritrovare Thomas Frank, suo ex allenatore al Brentford. Il centravanti sarebbe favorevole al trasferimento anche per rilanciare le proprie possibilità di convocazione in Nazionale in vista dell'Europeo 2028. Il Palace cerca un riferimento offensivo dopo un avvio di stagione complicato, con appena dieci reti nelle prime dieci giornate.

Infine, situazione da monitorare in casa Monaco. Folarin Balogun ha aperto alla possibilità di lasciare il Principato dopo il mancato trasferimento all'Everton della scorsa estate. L'attaccante statunitense, autore di un solo gol in sette presenze stagionali, sta trovando poco spazio e non esclude una nuova esperienza. Il tecnico Filipe Luis ha però ribadito la centralità del club rispetto ai singoli, chiedendo al giocatore maggiore concentrazione e disponibilità. Il futuro di Balogun resta dunque tutto da definire.

Penso che abbiamo fatto un ottimo primo tempo, la squadra non meritava di stare sotto. Non meritiamo questo passivo, non ricordo altre occasioni nitide della Lazio oltre i tre gol. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to reports from Italy, Liverpool are regularly scouting a red-hot striker who’s emerged as a shock candidate for the Golden Boot in Serie A this season.

Andoni Iraola has been almost exclusively reliant on Alexander Isak at centre-forward since taking charge of the Reds in the summer, with Hugo Ekitike continuing his recovery from a long-term Achilles injury.

The Frenchman is targeting a return to action next month (The Athletic), although it appears that Anfield chiefs are keeping tabs on a positional alternative who’s emerging as a breakthrough sensation in one of Europe’s major leagues.

A report from Corriere dello Sport has claimed that Liverpool are sending scouts ‘every week’ to watch Gustavo Varela, who’s been in remarkable goalscoring form with Monza since joining the Serie A outfit in the summer.

Napoli and Juventus have also been strongly linked with the 21-year-old, who’s been the subject of enquiries from Tottenham, Brentford and Sunderland, with the list of suitors growing in tandem with his goal return in the Italian top flight.

Ivan Juric’s side reportedly want €40m (£33.5m) for the Portuguese hitman, which’d represent a monumental profit on a player they signed from Gil Vicente in July for a paltry €2.5m (£2.1m).

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Varela is currently the leading scorer in Serie A this season with nine goals, which is remarkable when his team are currently in the relegation zone, and he accounts for more than half of their goal tally in the top flight so far.

Industry observers note that for someone who’d scored just seven times in 34 senior appearances before the summer, his form since joining Monza has been extraordinary. Should that continue, it’s safe to say that he won’t be at the Stadio Brianteo for much longer.

What Liverpool would need to consider is whether this is a mere purple patch from the Portuguese youngster, or the start of a journey towards being one of Europe’s most feared centre-forwards.

Varela has scored nine Serie A goals from an xG of just 5.48 (Fotmob), an astonishing overperformance which begs the question as to whether he can maintain that for a full campaign.

If Isak keeps up his own hot streak and Ekitike gets back to the levels he’d shown prior to his injury, it’d be difficult to see the Monza striker getting much of a look-in at Anfield.

However, it’s easy to see why Liverpool are routinely dispatching scouts to gather information on one of the breakout stars of European football in 2026.

Tech Report: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 33 min read (6619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~33 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.
  • Sources indicate that the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead.
  • That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

Sources indicate that the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

Industry observers note that as for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

Industry observers note that this was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

Sources indicate that in fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

Recent findings suggest that all that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be noted that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a substantial summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

Recent findings suggest that “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

Sources indicate that for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

In a recent development, A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

It has been revealed that chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

According to recent reports, “After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. It has been revealed that “It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

In a recent development, it is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

According to recent reports, “This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once stated of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. It has been revealed that A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

Recent findings suggest that the departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

Sources indicate that “We are better equipped,” stated Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

Recent findings suggest that asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

Industry observers note that “It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

According to recent reports, arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

In a recent development, “Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

Industry observers note that chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.
